note: Every setting says who decided it. 'decided' = the owner chose it. 'default' = the safe choice used until the owner decides. 'placeholder' = a number the assistant picked so that something runs; replace it with the owner's figure. 'open' = no value; goodlaw/pilot_settings.build_core refuses to run while any setting is open.

quiet_policy.decided_by: the owner, by telling the assistant to go with its recommendation
quiet_policy.reason: A case the checker found nothing against gets a grey line, 'No warning found in what we hold. This is not a finding that the case is good law.' Reasons: (1) the checker caught only about 3 in 10 verified overrulings, so a quiet card is weak evidence and the message should say so; (2) with no line, a quiet case looks the same as a message the formatter forgot to finish, and next to 'Not checked by us' it reads as 'checked, fine'; (3) the file export already spells a quiet case out, so chat and file agree; (4) on the 29 questions' hits only 2% were quiet cards (98% were not checked), so the line adds little to read. The risk is that some readers take the line as reassurance despite its words. Revisit after the first lawyers' marks: if passages under this line are often marked misleading, or lawyers say they read it as comfort, switch to 'silent' (a one-word change here).

keep_question_text.note: Off, so a client's name typed into a test question by mistake is not kept. Turning it on lets the marks sheet show the question beside each mark, which a reviewer would find easier; it needs the owner's decision and an Indian counsel's view on consent.

daily_question_cap.decided_by: the owner, in reply to the assistant's question of 2026-10-22 (read by the assistant as accepting the figures it had proposed; correct it here if that was not meant)
daily_question_cap.reason: Searches per user per day. At about $0.0004 a short question on rerank-3-lite (review_results/2026-10-22_pilot_cost/), ten a day for five people for 28 days is under $1 of Voyage credit; the figure is a limit on abuse and on a reviewer's reading load more than on cost.

global_daily_cap.decided_by: the owner, in reply to the assistant's question of 2026-10-22 (read by the assistant as accepting the figures it had proposed; correct it here if that was not meant)
global_daily_cap.reason: Searches for the whole test per day. At the maximum for 28 days this is about $1.18 of re-ranking on rerank-3-lite, against about $4.39 spendable above the owner's reserve (balance noted 2026-10-10, shared with the live site).

passages_shown.note: Passages shown per question. The earlier search review used the top 5 and top 10; three keeps a chat message list short.

rerank_model.decided_by: the owner, in reply to the assistant's question of 2026-10-22 ('1. rerank-3-lite')
rerank_model.reason: The re-ranker the pilot's search calls. Stage F's recorded spend is all rerank-3-lite (600,391 tokens for 29 questions), so the cost figures in review_results/2026-10-22_pilot_cost/ are for it; rerank-2 would cost 2.5 times as much. This setting does not switch anything by itself: nothing real is wired yet, and the search adapter, when it is built, reads this value.

max_question_chars.decided_by: the owner, in reply to the assistant's question of 2026-10-22 (read by the assistant as accepting the figures it had proposed; correct it here if that was not meant)
max_question_chars.reason: Longest question accepted, in characters. The re-ranker bills the question once for every candidate passage (60), so a 1,000-character question adds about 17,000 tokens to the usual 20,700: it roughly doubles the cost. A plain legal question is well under 500 characters. Longer ones are refused before anything is searched or recorded.

rules_version.note: The version of the three rules a user must accept. Change it when the rules change; everyone then accepts again.
